summary: Tenant throughput inversion and intermittent 5xx after hybrid async-batching + KV-prefetch + int8 quant — guided demotion and config audit
description:
Issue summary:
LumenDocs observed a sudden inversion in throughput and an increase in intermittent 5xx errors after enabling a combined optimization profile on their dedicated pool: async request-side batching + KV-prefetch + int8 quant profile. The configuration was rolled out to a subset of tenants last night (canary window) and expanded at 02:30 UTC — within an hour affected tenant latency P95 rose and error rate spiked. Customer service impact: document ingestion pipelines are intermittently failing and retries are amplifying traffic (risking quota exhaustion).

Impact:
- ~18% of requests for the tenant started returning 5xx within 45m of broadening the rollout.
- Tail latency (95th) jumped from ~220ms -> 1.2s for long-context (>1k tokens) requests.
- Throughput measured in requests/sec decreased by ~28% despite batch size increases ("throughput inversion").

Environment and recent change notes:
- Dedicated cluster: lumen-dedicated-pool-3 (us-east).
- Canary -> cluster-wide enable at 2026-03-10T02:30:00Z of profile: {async_batching: enabled (max_window_ms=40), kv_prefetch: enabled (hotset=20%), quant_profile: int8_auto}.
- No infra scaling events reported in cloud provider logs during the window.

Observed behavior vs expected:
- Observed: Increased contention on GPU kernels, frequent evictions of KV entries, longer lock/queue times in scheduler, and 5xx errors classified as "serving-timeout / kv-miss-burst".
- Expected: Higher token throughput and lower per-token cost with modest latency improvements for high-volume short requests.

Customer request:
- LumenDocs asked for an assisted audit and a safe, tenant-scoped demotion plan that minimizes downtime and avoids a full cluster rollback. They need stepwise guidance and a recommended ordering of demotion and validation checks.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) On a dedicated pool, enable async batching with max_window_ms=40 and kv_prefetch with hotset=20% for the tenant.
2) Apply int8_auto quant profile to model gpt-neo-2.7b-quant-int8.
3) Send a mixed stream of long-context ingestion requests (avg length 900-1500 tokens) at baseline rps.
4) Monitor serving-runtime metrics, scheduler queue times, and KV cache evictions.
Expected: Observe lower per-token latency and higher throughput; Reproduce the inversion: scheduler queue time increases and 5xx rate climbs with throughput drop.

investigation_notes:
Initial hypotheses considered:
- KV-prefetch + int8 quant may increase memory pressure leading to eviction churn; eviction storms can degrade performance when async batching grows batch size and memory working set.
- Async batching window tradeoff caused large variable batch sizes that increased GPU kernel switching overhead for long sequences, offsetting batching gains (throughput inversion).
- Scheduler backpressure and retry amplification resulted in extra queued work and transient 5xx.

What we checked so far:
- Confirmed no node-level OOMs.
- Observed elevated kernel-switch counts in runtime telemetry for tenant (kernel_switch_per_sec up ~3x).
- KV-prefetch hit-rate dropped from 84% -> 61% after rollout.
- Request retry rate increased by ~2.6x when batch size exceeded 16.

Quick mitigations tried by customer before ticket:
- Reduced async max_window_ms to 20ms (helped short requests but long-context still affected).
- Temporarily disabled inter-tenant traffic shaping (no measurable effect).

Support notes / immediate priority:
- Avoid cluster-wide rollback. Prefer per-tenant staged demotion with telemetry gates and a short stabilization window (5-10 minutes) per step.
recommended_rollback_procedure:
High-level safe demotion (tenant-scoped):
1) Stage 0 - Circuit gate: apply rate-limit cap for tenant to prevent retry storms (set tenant.rps_cap = baseline * 1.1). Monitor for 3 minutes.
2) Stage 1 - Demote KV-prefetch to 'read-only' (effectively disable proactive prefetch) for tenant: toggles: kv_prefetch.enabled=false. Observe kv_hit_rate, eviction_rate for 5 minutes. If 5xx falls and p95 improves, keep demotion.
3) Stage 2 - Reduce async batching aggressiveness: set async_batching.max_window_ms=10 and max_batch_size=8 for tenant. Monitor queue_time_ms and kernel_switch_per_sec for 10 minutes.
4) Stage 3 - If issues persist, revert quant profile to float16-fallback for that tenant: quant_profile=int16_safe. Validate that model warms up and token accuracy checks pass.
5) Stage 4 - If still degraded, snapshot tenant config and perform a safe snapshot-restore to last-known-good config and optionally split traffic to a non-optimized variant (traffic_split=90/10 non-optimized).
6) Post-mortem: capture full trace windows and run the provided profiling harness against a representative request set.
Notes: Execute Stages sequentially with telemetry gates; do not skip Stage 1 (KV demotion) as eviction churn is likely the dominant contributor. Each stage should include a 5-10 minute stabilization window and a rollback button to re-enable the previous setting.
Suggested CLI snippets: 
- Disable kv-prefetch: redwoodctl tenants update --tenant-id lumen-42 --set \"optimizer.kv_prefetch.enabled=false\"
- Reduce async window: redwoodctl tenants update --tenant-id lumen-42 --set \"optimizer.async_batching.max_window_ms=10\" --set \"optimizer.async_batching.max_batch_size=8\"
- Revert quant: redwoodctl models update --model-id gpt-neo-2.7b-quant-int8 --set \"quant_profile=float16_safe\" --tenant-scope lumen-42
comments: 2026-03-10T09:12 Maya Chen (Support): Customer reported spike; attached telemetry snapshot and mentioned they enabled optimization profile during low-traffic hours — expanded at 02:30 UTC.

2026-03-10T10:05 Lina Rodriguez (SRE): I've started a live audit on lumen-dedicated-pool-3. Beginning with eviction metrics and kernel switch telemetry. Planning staged demotion as described in investigation notes.

2026-03-10T10:23 LumenDocs (Customer): We see the same timelines; please advise which toggle to flip first — KV or batching?
Customer also asked whether a quant revert risks accuracy regressions on verified prompts.

2026-03-10T10:35 Lina Rodriguez (SRE): Recommend KV-prefetch demotion first. Quant revert to float16_safe is low risk for short term; accuracy delta expected <0.5% on our eval suite but please run customer acceptance tests. Linking profiling PR: github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/3192 for additional telemetry knobs.

2026-03-11T01:50 Maya Chen (Support): Customer executed Stage 1 (kv_prefetch disabled). Early telemetry shows kv_hit_rate up to 76% and eviction_rate down; p95 trending down after 7 minutes. Awaiting 30m stability window before next stage.

2026-03-12T07:14 Lina Rodriguez (SRE): Post-stage summary: after completing Stage 2 adjustments (reduced async window) the tenant returned to expected throughput. Recommended follow-ups in resolution below.
resolution:
Staged demotion executed with support:
- Stage 1 disabled kv_prefetch for tenant lumen-42; eviction storms subsided.
- Stage 2 reduced async batching window and max_batch_size; scheduler queue_time and kernel_switch_per_sec normalized.
- No full-quant revert required; team kept quant_profile unchanged after validation (float16-safe remains an available fallback).
Follow-up actions:
- Run a 48-hour regression run against customer prompt sets with current optimization settings.
- Add a canary safety gate: when enabling combined optimization profiles, the platform will enforce automated telemetry gates (kv_hit_rate and kernel_switch thresholds) and block rollout if thresholds exceeded.
- Create a small runbook snippet in Confluence for tenant-scoped demotion (linked).
Ticket status: monitoring period started; recommended to keep ticket open until 2026-03-14 for final verification and CJ sign-off.
